set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Floor puzzle
set.stimulus:
Eight persons — J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q — live on eight different floors of a building, one person on each floor, but not necessarily in the same order. The lowermost floor is numbered 1 and the topmost floor is numbered 8. Each of them likes a different flower — Lotus, Daisy, Sunflower, Lily, Rose, Tulip, Orchid and Jasmine.

1. Neither M nor the one who likes Tulip lives on a prime-numbered floor.
2. The one who likes Rose lives immediately below the one who likes Lily.
3. As many persons live below the one who likes Orchid as above N.
4. Only six persons live below Q.
5. Less than two persons live above the one who likes Rose.
6. Only three persons live between L and the one who likes Daisy.
7. O likes Lily.
8. Less than three persons live between K and the one who likes Rose.
9. As many persons live below N as above L.
10. J does not like Daisy.
11. K does not like Tulip.
12. Neither J nor the one who likes Orchid lives on the lowermost floor.
13. Only three persons live between the one who likes Sunflower and the one who likes Lotus, and the one who likes Sunflower lives above the one who likes Lotus.
14. The one who likes Jasmine does not live immediately above or immediately below the one who likes Lotus.

Case the one who likes Rose on floor 8: clue 2 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Rose on floor 7 survives.
Clue 2 → the one who likes Lily on floor 8; Clue 7 → O on floor 8.
Now the one who likes Orchid can be on floor 2, floor 3, floor 4, floor 5 or floor 6 (clue 12) — make 5 cases.
Case the one who likes Orchid on floor 2: clue 3 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Orchid on floor 3: clue 6 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Orchid on floor 4: clue 6 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Orchid on floor 5: no place is left for the one who likes Lotus — rejected.
Case the one who likes Orchid on floor 6 survives.
Clue 3 → N on floor 3; Clue 9 → L on floor 6.
Clue 6 → the one who likes Daisy on floor 2; P can only be on floor 2 (every other place is ruled out).
The same clues then place M (floor 1).
Now the one who likes Lotus can be on floor 1, floor 3, floor 4 or floor 5 — make 4 cases.
Case the one who likes Lotus on floor 3: clue 13 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Lotus on floor 4: clue 13 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Lotus on floor 5: clue 13 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the one who likes Lotus on floor 1 survives.
Clue 13 → the one who likes Sunflower on floor 5; The one who likes Tulip takes the only place left: floor 4.
The one who likes Jasmine takes the only place left: floor 3; Clues 8 and 11 → K on floor 5.
The same clues then place J (floor 4).
Final arrangement (top to bottom): O, Q, L, K, J, N, P, M.
M is on floor 1, so the place immediately above is floor 2 → **P**.

solution.trap: **J** fits only if clue 1 is ignored.
